Initiate the movement slowly through the prescribed range.
Hold the end-range briefly and contract the target muscle.
Return under control to the starting position.

progressions: Increase load by 5–10% when current dose feels RPE ≤6
Add unilateral or unstable surface variation
Increase range of motion or tempo
Add sport-/task-specific complexity
regressions: Reduce range of motion to a pain-free arc
Remove load (bodyweight only) or use assistance (band/TRX)
Slow tempo and add brief end-range pauses
Perform in a more stable position (supine, supported)

"Drive through the floor"
"Long spine, soft knees"
"Breathe into your back, not your shoulders"

Loss of neutral spine at end range
Compensating with adjacent joint
Using momentum instead of muscular control

description: Strengthening exercise targeting Hamstrings in the Lower Extremity region.
instructions: Machine seated hamstring curl through full ROM.
clinical_notes: Isolated hamstring strengthening. Good for early rehab.
starting_position: Adopt a neutral, well-supported position appropriate to the movement; brace core lightly before initiating.
execution_steps: Set up in the described starting position with controlled breathing.
Initiate the movement slowly through the prescribed range.
Hold the end-range briefly and contract the target muscle.
Return under control to the starting position.
breathing: Exhale on the concentric (effort) phase, inhale on the eccentric (return) phase. Avoid breath-holding.
load_dosage: 3–4 sets × 6–12 reps at RPE 7–8, 2–3×/week, 48 h between sessions.
progressions: Increase load by 5–10% when current dose feels RPE ≤6
Add unilateral or unstable surface variation
Increase range of motion or tempo
Add sport-/task-specific complexity
regressions: Reduce range of motion to a pain-free arc
Remove load (bodyweight only) or use assistance (band/TRX)
Slow tempo and add brief end-range pauses
Perform in a more stable position (supine, supported)
cueing: "Stack ribs over pelvis"
"Drive through the floor"
"Long spine, soft knees"
"Breathe into your back, not your shoulders"
common_errors: Holding breath under load
Loss of neutral spine at end range
Compensating with adjacent joint
Using momentum instead of muscular control
contraindications: Acute, severe pain (>7/10)
Recent post-op restrictions not yet cleared
Active joint inflammation with effusion
Unstable fracture or ligamentous instability
references: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription (11e, 2021)

clinical_notes: Intermediate functional for Core rehabilitation. Progress when pain ≤2/10 during loading and 24-h symptom recovery.
starting_position: Adopt a neutral, well-supported position appropriate to the movement; brace core lightly before initiating.
execution_steps: Set up in the described starting position with controlled breathing.
Initiate the movement slowly through the prescribed range.
Hold the end-range briefly and contract the target muscle.
Return under control to the starting position.
breathing: Exhale on the concentric (effort) phase, inhale on the eccentric (return) phase. Avoid breath-holding.
tempo: Slow and controlled, ~3–5 s per rep
progressions: Increase load by 5–10% when current dose feels RPE ≤6
Add unilateral or unstable surface variation
Increase range of motion or tempo
Add sport-/task-specific complexity
regressions: Reduce range of motion to a pain-free arc
Remove load (bodyweight only) or use assistance (band/TRX)
Slow tempo and add brief end-range pauses
Perform in a more stable position (supine, supported)
cueing: "Stack ribs over pelvis"
"Drive through the floor"
"Long spine, soft knees"
"Breathe into your back, not your shoulders"
common_errors: Holding breath under load
Loss of neutral spine at end range
Compensating with adjacent joint
Using momentum instead of muscular control
contraindications: Acute, severe pain (>7/10)
Recent post-op restrictions not yet cleared
Active joint inflammation with effusion
Unstable fracture or ligamentous instability
references: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription (11e, 2021)

instructions: Use bodyweight in standing/weight-bearing position. Cue Pronator Teres engagement during functional task.
clinical_notes: Improves transfer of strength to ADLs. Combine with proprioceptive challenge for return-to-sport.
starting_position: Adopt a neutral, well-supported position appropriate to the movement; brace core lightly before initiating.
execution_steps: Use bodyweight in standing/weight-bearing position
Cue Pronator Teres engagement during functional task
breathing: Exhale on the concentric (effort) phase, inhale on the eccentric (return) phase. Avoid breath-holding.
tempo: Slow and controlled, ~3–5 s per rep
load_dosage: 3 x 10 reps
progressions: Increase load by 5–10% when current dose feels RPE ≤6
Add unilateral or unstable surface variation
Increase range of motion or tempo
Add sport-/task-specific complexity
regressions: Reduce range of motion to a pain-free arc
Remove load (bodyweight only) or use assistance (band/TRX)
Slow tempo and add brief end-range pauses
Perform in a more stable position (supine, supported)
cueing: "Stack ribs over pelvis"
"Drive through the floor"
"Long spine, soft knees"
"Breathe into your back, not your shoulders"
common_errors: Holding breath under load
Loss of neutral spine at end range
Compensating with adjacent joint
Using momentum instead of muscular control
contraindications: Acute, severe pain (>7/10)
Recent post-op restrictions not yet cleared
Active joint inflammation with effusion
Unstable fracture or ligamentous instability
references: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription (11e, 2021)
Kisner & Colby — Therapeutic Exercise (7e, 2017)

description: Sub-maximal isometric loading of Wrist Flexors.
instructions: Place Wrist Flexors at mid-range. Push against an immovable resistance at ~70% effort. Breathe normally.
clinical_notes: Mid-stage progression — monitor symptoms 24 h post-session.
starting_position: Adopt a neutral, well-supported position appropriate to the plate pinch hold; brace core lightly before initiating.
execution_steps: Set up in the described starting position with controlled breathing.
Initiate the movement focusing on Wrist Flexors activation.
Move through the prescribed range under control.
Return slowly to the starting position; reset for next rep.
breathing: Exhale on the concentric (effort) phase, inhale on the eccentric (return) phase. Avoid breath-holding.
tempo: Ramp to target force over 2 s; hold; relax 30 s.
load_dosage: 70% MVC × 5 × 10 s; rest 30 s; 2–3×/day for early-stage tendon/painful loading.
progressions: Increase load by 5–10% when current dose feels RPE ≤6
Add unilateral or unstable surface variation
Increase range of motion or tempo
Add sport-/task-specific complexity
regressions: Reduce range of motion to a pain-free arc
Remove load (bodyweight only) or use assistance (band/TRX)
Slow tempo and add brief end-range pauses
Perform in a more stable position (supine, supported)
cueing: "Feel the wrist flexors working"
"Long spine, soft knees"
"Breathe — don't hold your breath"
"Control the return"
common_errors: Holding breath under load
Loss of neutral spine / posture at end range
Compensating with adjacent joint
Using momentum instead of muscular control
contraindications: Acute, severe pain (>7/10)
Recent post-op restrictions not yet cleared
Active joint inflammation with effusion
Unstable fracture or ligamentous instability
references: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription (11e, 2021)
Kisner & Colby — Therapeutic Exercise (7e, 2017)

instructions: Hinge 45°, drive elbows past ribs. Anchor the band so resistance peaks at end range.
sets_reps: 3–4 sets × 12 reps with a medium band, 3×/week, RPE 6
load_dosage: 3–4 sets × 12 reps with a medium band, 3×/week, RPE 6
clinical_notes: Indicated for Posterior chain weakness. Progress only when the current dose is completed with ≤2/10 pain that settles within 24 h.
starting_position: Set up for bent-over row in a stable, well-supported position with the thoracic spine in neutral alignment.
execution_steps: Adopt the described starting position and set the latissimus dorsi.
Hinge 45°, drive elbows past ribs.
Anchor the band so resistance peaks at end range.
Return under control and reset alignment before the next repetition.
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on the return. Never hold the breath (avoid Valsalva).
progressions: Increase band tension or load 5–10% once the top of the rep range feels RPE ≤6
Progress to a single-limb or longer-lever version
Add tempo, pause, or plyometric demand in the final phase
regressions: Reduce range to the pain-free arc
Drop to bodyweight or a lighter band
Convert to an isometric hold at the least painful angle
cueing: Hinge 45°, drive elbows past ribs.
Anchor the band so resistance peaks at end range.
Keep the movement smooth — quality over quantity.
common_errors: Compensating with adjacent segments instead of the target muscle
Rushing the eccentric phase
Progressing load before technique is consistent
contraindications: Acute unhealed fracture or post-op precaution phase
Pain >5/10 during or lasting >24 h after the session
Active infection, DVT or unexplained red-flag symptoms
references: ACSM resistance-training guidance 2021
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

instructions: Open fingers wide against resistance. Work strictly within the pain-free arc.
load_dosage: 2–3 sets × 10–15 reps daily, RPE 2–3
clinical_notes: Indicated for Extensor imbalance. Progress only when the current dose is completed with ≤2/10 pain that settles within 24 h.
starting_position: Set up for finger extension against band in a stable, well-supported position with the wrist/hand in neutral alignment.
execution_steps: Adopt the described starting position and set the extensor digitorum.
Open fingers wide against resistance.
Work strictly within the pain-free arc.
Return under control and reset alignment before the next repetition.
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on the return. Never hold the breath (avoid Valsalva).
progressions: Increase band tension or load 5–10% once the top of the rep range feels RPE ≤6
Progress to a single-limb or longer-lever version
Add tempo, pause, or plyometric demand in the final phase
regressions: Reduce range to the pain-free arc
Drop to bodyweight or a lighter band
Convert to an isometric hold at the least painful angle
cueing: Open fingers wide against resistance.
Work strictly within the pain-free arc.
Keep the movement smooth — quality over quantity.
common_errors: Compensating with adjacent segments instead of the target muscle
Rushing the eccentric phase
Progressing load before technique is consistent
contraindications: Acute unhealed fracture or post-op precaution phase
Pain >5/10 during or lasting >24 h after the session
Active infection, DVT or unexplained red-flag symptoms

ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

instructions: Press knee down, tighten thigh 5 s. Control the return phase — do not let the band snap back.
sets_reps: 4 sets × 8–10 reps with a heavy band, 3×/week, RPE 7–8
load_dosage: 4 sets × 8–10 reps with a heavy band, 3×/week, RPE 7–8
clinical_notes: Indicated for Post-op knee, quad inhibition. Progress only when the current dose is completed with ≤2/10 pain that settles within 24 h.
starting_position: Set up for quadriceps setting in a stable, well-supported position with the knee in neutral alignment.
execution_steps: Adopt the described starting position and set the vastus medialis.
Press knee down, tighten thigh 5 s.
Control the return phase — do not let the band snap back.
Return under control and reset alignment before the next repetition.
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on the return. Never hold the breath (avoid Valsalva).
tempo: 3-1-3 controlled, or explosive concentric where prescribed
progressions: Increase band tension or load 5–10% once the top of the rep range feels RPE ≤6
Progress to a single-limb or longer-lever version
Add tempo, pause, or plyometric demand in the final phase
regressions: Reduce range to the pain-free arc
Drop to bodyweight or a lighter band
Convert to an isometric hold at the least painful angle
cueing: Press knee down, tighten thigh 5 s.
Control the return phase — do not let the band snap back.
Keep the movement smooth — quality over quantity.
common_errors: Compensating with adjacent segments instead of the target muscle
Rushing the eccentric phase
Progressing load before technique is consistent
contraindications: Acute unhealed fracture or post-op precaution phase
Pain >5/10 during or lasting >24 h after the session
Active infection, DVT or unexplained red-flag symptoms
references: Logerstedt et al., JOSPT 2018
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

Convert to an isometric hold at the least painful angle

instructions: Tall posture, knee to hip height. Own the full range before adding load.
load_dosage: 3 sets × 12–15 reps, 3–4×/week, RPE 4–5
clinical_notes: Indicated for Deconditioning, warm-up. Progress only when the current dose is completed with ≤2/10 pain that settles within 24 h.
starting_position: Set up for marching in place in a stable, well-supported position with the full body in neutral alignment.
execution_steps: Adopt the described starting position and set the hip flexors.
Tall posture, knee to hip height.
Own the full range before adding load.
Return under control and reset alignment before the next repetition.
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on the return. Never hold the breath (avoid Valsalva).
progressions: Increase band tension or load 5–10% once the top of the rep range feels RPE ≤6
Progress to a single-limb or longer-lever version
Add tempo, pause, or plyometric demand in the final phase
regressions: Reduce range to the pain-free arc
Drop to bodyweight or a lighter band
Convert to an isometric hold at the least painful angle
cueing: Tall posture, knee to hip height.
Own the full range before adding load.
Keep the movement smooth — quality over quantity.
common_errors: Compensating with adjacent segments instead of the target muscle
Rushing the eccentric phase
Progressing load before technique is consistent
contraindications: Acute unhealed fracture or post-op precaution phase
Pain >5/10 during or lasting >24 h after the session
Active infection, DVT or unexplained red-flag symptoms
references: Sherrington et al., Cochrane 2019
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

clinical_notes: Indicated for Elderly power. Progress only when the current dose is completed with ≤2/10 pain that settles within 24 h.

execution_steps: Adopt the described starting position and set the quadriceps.
Stand fully then rise on toes.
Band tension should be even through the whole range.
Return under control and reset alignment before the next repetition.
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on the return. Never hold the breath (avoid Valsalva).
progressions: Increase band tension or load 5–10% once the top of the rep range feels RPE ≤6
Progress to a single-limb or longer-lever version
Add tempo, pause, or plyometric demand in the final phase
regressions: Reduce range to the pain-free arc
Drop to bodyweight or a lighter band
Convert to an isometric hold at the least painful angle
cueing: Stand fully then rise on toes.
Band tension should be even through the whole range.
Keep the movement smooth — quality over quantity.
common_errors: Compensating with adjacent segments instead of the target muscle
Rushing the eccentric phase
Progressing load before technique is consistent
contraindications: Acute unhealed fracture or post-op precaution phase
Pain >5/10 during or lasting >24 h after the session
Active infection, DVT or unexplained red-flag symptoms
